introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Differentiate between renewable energy sources and non-renewable energy sources, giving one example in each case. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Renewable energy sources** are sources that are **replenished by natural processes at a rate comparable with (or faster than) the rate at which they are used**, so that they cannot be exhausted on a human time scale. Example: **solar energy** (also wind, hydroelectric, tidal, biomass or geothermal energy).

**Non-renewable energy sources** are sources that exist in a **finite stock**, which is being used much faster than it is formed (it takes millions of years), so that it will eventually run out. Example: **coal** (also oil, natural gas or nuclear fuel such as uranium).

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) For a wind mill, the kinetic energy per unit time, $P = \dfrac{1}{2}\pi r^2\rho v^3$ where $r$ is the radius of the blades, $\rho$ the density of air and $v$ the speed of the wind. The diameter of the blades of an aero-generator of the mill is $4\ \mathrm{m}$. What is the power output of the wind mill on a day when air has a density of $1.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$ and the wind is blowing with a velocity of $144\ \mathrm{km}$ per hour if the efficiency of the wind mill is $25\%$? *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Data.** Radius $r = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2\ \mathrm{m}$; $\rho = 1.2\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$; wind speed
$$v = 144\ \mathrm{km\,h^{-1}} = \frac{144\times1000}{3600} = 40\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.$$

**Kinetic energy per unit time of the wind passing through the blades.**
$$P = \tfrac12\pi r^2\rho v^3 = \tfrac12\times\pi\times(2)^2\times1.2\times(40)^3 = \tfrac12\times\pi\times4\times1.2\times64000$$
$$P = 4.83\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{W}.$$

**Electrical power output** (efficiency $25\% = 0.25$):
$$P_{\text{out}} = 0.25\times4.83\times10^{5} = 1.21\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{W}.$$

**The power output is about $1.2\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{W}$ ($121\ \mathrm{kW}$).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Draw an energy-flow diagram of a hydroelectric power plant. *[3 marks]*

(ii) State one environmental problem that arises from the construction of a hydroelectric power plant. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Energy-flow diagram (to be drawn by the candidate).** The energy transformations, each shown by an arrow in the diagram, are:

$$\text{gravitational potential energy of the water in the dam (reservoir)}$$
$$\downarrow\ \text{water falls through the penstock (pipe)}$$
$$\text{kinetic energy of the fast-moving water}$$
$$\downarrow\ \text{water strikes the turbine blades}$$
$$\text{rotational kinetic energy of the turbine}$$
$$\downarrow\ \text{the turbine drives the generator}$$
$$\text{electrical energy (transmitted by the grid)}$$

At each stage a part of the energy is **wasted** as heat and sound (friction in the pipes, turbine and generator bearings, resistance of the windings), shown by side arrows. Total energy is conserved: the electrical output plus the wasted energy equals the initial potential energy.

**(ii) One environmental problem.** The dam **floods a large area of land upstream**, destroying forests, farmland and the habitats of animals and plants, and forcing people to move. (Other acceptable answers: blocking the migration of fish and changing the flow of the river downstream; rotting vegetation in the reservoir releasing methane; trapping silt behind the dam.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Explain what is meant by global warming.

(ii) State and explain one effect of global warming on human beings. *[4 marks for (d)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Global warming.** Global warming is the **gradual increase of the average temperature of the earth's atmosphere and oceans**. It is caused mainly by the **enhanced greenhouse effect**: burning fossil fuels and deforestation raise the concentration of greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide, methane, ...) in the atmosphere. These gases let the short-wavelength radiation from the sun pass through but **absorb the infrared radiation emitted by the warm earth** and re-radiate part of it back towards the surface, so the earth retains more energy.

**(ii) One effect on human beings.** **Rise in sea level.** Warming melts glaciers and ice caps and makes the ocean water expand thermally; the sea level rises, so low-lying coastal regions and cities are **flooded**, farmland is salted, and people living there are **displaced**.

(Other acceptable answers: more frequent heat waves, floods and droughts that damage crops and cause famine; wider spread of diseases such as malaria.)
